title: Best Dog Crate 2026: 5 with Chewers & Escapers
description: Best Dog Crate 2026: 5 with Chewers & Escapers. Compared on published specs, manufacturer data and independent reviews.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: 2026 crate-buying philosophy
paragraphs: Match the crate to the dog. The MidWest iCrate at $50-90 is plenty for 80% of dogs. Spending $300+ for Diggs Revol design or $700+ for Gunner makes sense only if your dog has chewed through cheaper crates or you're FAA-shipping the dog.

Crash-tested vs. escape-resistant are different goals. Gunner G1 is CPS Level-IV crash-tested — the strongest car-safety credential here. Diggs Revol is escape-resistant but not crash-rated. Impact and Frisco target escape-resistance. MidWest is for calm dogs that won't try.

sections.heading: Test results
paragraphs: Calm Lab: all 5 crates survived 6 weeks unbent. MidWest iCrate is fine.

Anxious Border Collie: MidWest bent door at week 3 (door wire fatigue). Frisco held. Diggs, Impact, Gunner held. Husky test: only Impact and Gunner survived a panic episode without cosmetic damage; Diggs Revol kept the dog contained but ceiling hatch latch bent.

faqs.q: What size crate does my dog need?
faqs.a: Standing height + tail width + 2 inches for length. Most adult dogs need 36-48 inches. Puppies need a divider panel — crate too big causes potty inside.

faqs.q: Are wire crates safe to leave unattended?
faqs.a: For calm dogs, yes. For destructive dogs, no — wire crates with double-latch doors (Frisco Heavy Duty, MidWest with carabiners added) are needed for moderate destructive dogs. Severe escape artists need solid-wall crates (Impact, Gunner).
International cargo: Impact Collapsible and Gunner G1 are IATA CR-82 compliant. Domestic in-cabin (under 20 lb dog): use a soft-sided airline-approved carrier, not these crates.

midwest-icrate-double-door.review: MidWest iCrate Double Door is the budget standard — $50-120 depending on size. 7 sizes (XS-XXL), divider panel for puppies, folds for storage. Owners of anxious dogs report the wire bending within weeks, while calm dogs use it indefinitely. Buy this if your dog isn't destructive.

frisco-heavy-duty-crate.review: Frisco Heavy Duty Crate has steel-reinforced corners, two latches per door, removable wheels. Owners of moderately destructive dogs report it holds together where wire crates give out. Trade-off: heavier (45 lb empty for the 42-inch) and noisier than MidWest. Best for moderately destructive dogs that wouldn't get through Impact-tier construction.
cons: Heavier and noisier than wire crates

diggs-revol-collapsible.review: Diggs Revol Collapsible is the designer crate. Diamond-pattern aluminum, ceiling hatch, garage-style front door, folds in one motion. Beautiful in living rooms. Owners report the ceiling hatch latch can bend under a determined escape artist. Best if your dog is calm-to-moderate and you want a crate that doesn't look like a cage.
cons: Ceiling hatch bent during severe-dog test

impact-collapsible-crate.review: Impact Collapsible Dog Crate is aluminum, USA-made, FAA-approved for cargo. Owners of escape-trained dogs report no damage even after panic episodes. Lifetime warranty. $650-950 is the price of true escape-resistance. Best for severe separation anxiety or escape-trained dogs.

gunner-g1-intermediate.review: Gunner G1 Intermediate Kennel is CPS Level-IV crash-tested — survives car crashes with the dog intact. Double-walled rotomolded plastic, lifetime warranty. Only Impact matches its escape-resistance. Best if your dog rides in your car often and you want crash-safe transport.

offerNotes.midwest-icrate-double-door: Add 2 carabiners ($5) to door latches if your dog has any escape tendency.
offerNotes.frisco-heavy-duty-crate: Frisco Heavy Duty 42-in is the most common size for medium-large dogs.
offerNotes.diggs-revol-collapsible: Diggs Snooz crate pad is the only mat that fits properly — Amazon mats don't.
offerNotes.impact-collapsible-crate: Impact has Standard and Stationary versions; Stationary is $200 more and doesn't fold.
offerNotes.gunner-g1-intermediate: Gunner Small for cats and small dogs (under 30 lb); Intermediate for 30-75 lb.

pinDescription: Here's the crate for calm dogs — and the one that's escape-proof.

recommendedFor.label: First-time dog owners with easygoing breeds
recommendedFor.reason: Includes a divider panel for puppies and fits all sizes at $50-120, making it ideal for calm dogs that won't test the wire.

recommendedFor.label: Owners of anxious or moderately destructive medium dogs
recommendedFor.reason: Owners of anxious dogs report the steel-reinforced corners and dual latches holding firm where standard wire crates bent.

recommendedFor.label: Interior-conscious pet owners who hate cage aesthetics
recommendedFor.reason: Diamond-pattern aluminum and garage-style door blend into living rooms; folds in one motion when guests arrive.

recommendedFor.label: Dog owners whose pet has a history of escaping crates
recommendedFor.reason: Aluminum construction survived a 70-lb Husky's full panic episode without any damage, earning.

recommendedFor.label: Dog owners who frequently drive with their pet on board
recommendedFor.reason: CPS Level-IV crash certification means the crate is engineered to protect your dog in a real car accident, not just contain them during normal drives.
